01 / ORIENT8 min

Understand the tools

You don’t need to learn everything before you start. Begin with who does what.

ChatGPT & Codex

ChatGPT is an AI assistant you can talk to. Codex is a coding agent that can inspect a project, edit files and run checks when its tools and permissions allow.

Git & GitHub

Git tracks versions of files on your computer. GitHub hosts repositories online so teammates can access and collaborate on them.

Agentic AI works through several steps toward a goal, using tools and checking results. You still decide the goal, review changes and judge whether the result works. A code editor helps you read and change code; a terminal runs typed commands.

Your pocket Git vocabulary
Repository (repo)
A project’s files plus their tracked history.
Clone
Make a local copy of an online repository, including its history.
Branch
A separate line of work within a repository.
Commit
A named snapshot of selected changes, saved locally.
Push
Upload local commits to the remote repository.
Pull
Fetch remote changes and integrate them into your current branch.
Two distinctions worth keeping.

AI can build an ordinary website. That does not mean the website uses AI when someone visits. Our agenda tool needs no AI connection.

Connecting your GitHub account to an app grants that app access. Cloning a repository connects a local project copy to its remote. These are separate steps.

Read more: OpenAI quickstart · Git basics

02 / PREPARE10 min + installation

Prepare your workspace

Already set up? Run the checks, mark what you’ve completed and move on. Setup friction is normal; it is information, not a verdict on your ability.

1. Check account access

Sign in at ChatGPT and GitHub. Confirm you are using the account your team will invite. In ChatGPT, try asking: “Explain a Git commit in two sentences for a beginner.” Read the reply critically.

Follow the official desktop quickstart to install the version for your computer and sign in with your ChatGPT account. Select Codex for this coding exercise. Current documentation calls the desktop app ChatGPT; classmates may still see Codex branding. Labels, availability and limits vary by app version, account and workspace policy. Check your own access before buying anything; ask your instructor or workspace administrator if access is missing.

2. Install only what this exercise uses

You need a browser, the desktop coding app and Git. A separate code editor is optional if you can inspect files in the app. Our plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript exercise does not require Python, Node.js or an API key. Other projects may need Python to run Python code, Node.js for JavaScript build tools, or an API key to call a paid API. Install those only when the project actually requires them.

Open Windows Search, type PowerShell, and open Windows PowerShell. Microsoft instructions.

If Git is missing, use the official Git for Windows installer, then close and reopen PowerShell.

Open Terminal from Applications → Utilities. Apple’s Terminal guide.

If Git is missing, run xcode-select --install in Terminal and follow the installer for Apple’s Command Line Tools. Then reopen Terminal. Git’s macOS installation options.

RUN IN POWERSHELL / TERMINAL
git --version

Expected: a line beginning “git version”. The exact number may differ.

If this fails: finish the Git installation and reopen your terminal. On a managed computer, ask IT for installation help.

Next: Connect with your team →
03 / CONNECT12 min

Connect with your team

Choose the path that matches your role. Everyone then clones the same repository.

I’m creating the team repository
  1. On GitHub, use the upper-right + menu → New repository. Name it mld371-agenda.
  2. Choose Private for team-only source access unless your team agrees otherwise. Public means anyone can read the source. Initialize with a README, then create the repository.
  3. For a personal repository, open Settings → Collaborators → Add people. Invite teammates by their GitHub usernames. Organization repositories may use different access controls and require admin help.

Create a repository · Invite collaborators

I’m joining a teammate’s repository
  1. Ask the owner to invite your exact GitHub username.
  2. Sign into that account and accept the invitation from the GitHub email or invitation link provided by the owner.
  3. Open the repository link. You should see its README. If you cannot, ask the owner to check whether the invitation is still pending and whether it grants write access.

Clone once, then use that folder

On the repository page, choose Code → Local → HTTPS and copy the URL. Pick a parent folder on your computer where the new project should live. The following paths are examples: replace YOUR_NAME with your own folder name. Choose a folder that already exists.

EDIT FIRST · RUN IN POWERSHELL
cd "C:\Users\YOUR_NAME\Documents"
EDIT FIRST · RUN IN TERMINAL
cd "/Users/YOUR_NAME/Documents"

Replace TEAM_OWNER below with the actual owner from the copied URL. Do not type the sample unchanged.

EDIT FIRST · RUN IN POWERSHELL / TERMINAL
git clone https://github.com/TEAM_OWNER/mld371-agenda.git
cd mld371-agenda
git rev-parse --show-toplevel
git remote -v

Expected: a project folder ending in mld371-agenda and an origin URL matching your team’s repository.

If this fails: “already exists” means check the existing folder before cloning again. “Repository not found” can mean a wrong URL, wrong signed-in account or missing permission. See lesson 4.

In the desktop app, open that exact project folder and start a new Codex task in it. Choose local work in the selected folder if the app offers an environment choice. Ask the agent to confirm its working folder before editing. OpenAI folder setup · GitHub cloning guide

Choose the parent of .git. The hidden .git directory stores history. Select mld371-agenda, which contains it—not .git itself.
Next: Untangle setup →
04 / TROUBLESHOOT8 min or as needed

A small check before a big fix

If something feels wrong, pause and compare paths and accounts. Open the symptom that matches. These checks inspect your setup without changing it.

RUN IN THE PROJECT · POWERSHELL / TERMINAL
pwd
git rev-parse --show-toplevel
git remote -v
git status -sb
My files are missing, or I see a similarly named folder

Meaning: you may be in a different copy. Check: compare the full path from pwd and git rev-parse --show-toplevel with the folder selected in Codex; compare the remote with GitHub. Smallest fix: open the verified clone in the app and terminal. Keep other copies until you have checked whether they contain unique work. “Not a git repository” means the current folder is not inside the clone.

Windows shows two Documents folders

Meaning: local Documents and OneDrive Documents can be different locations. Check: compare full paths such as C:\Users\YOUR_NAME\Documents\mld371-agenda and C:\Users\YOUR_NAME\OneDrive\Documents\mld371-agenda. Your organization’s OneDrive name may differ. Smallest fix: select the same verified path in both apps. Do not move or delete folders to guess your way out. Microsoft explains OneDrive folder backup.

I selected .git and can’t see my project

Meaning: you opened Git’s internal history folder. Check: does the selected path end in \.git or /.git? Smallest fix: go up one level and select the parent project folder. Do not delete .git.

GitHub is connected in the app, but clone or push fails

Meaning: an app connector and command-line Git can use separate authentication. Check: confirm the HTTPS remote and the account with repository access. Smallest fix: follow GitHub’s HTTPS credential-manager or SSH setup for your chosen remote; for this HTTPS path, a credential manager can offer browser sign-in. A GitHub account password is not an HTTPS Git credential. Never paste tokens into chat, code or a remote URL. GitHub authentication guide.

Codex keeps referring to the old project

Meaning: the old conversation may still use its original folder or context. Check: ask it to report its current working directory and repository remote without editing anything. Smallest fix: select the intended clone and start a fresh task there. Switching the sidebar selection is not proof that an existing task changed folders.

I committed, but teammates can’t see the change

Meaning: a commit is still local until pushed. Check: git status -sb may show “ahead”; compare git log -1 --oneline with the correct branch on GitHub. Smallest fix: push that branch, then refresh GitHub and compare the commit again. A clean working tree alone does not prove upload.

The repository is “not found” or push says permission denied

Meaning: the URL, account or access may be wrong. Check: open the exact repository in your browser while signed into the invited account. Ask the owner to check pending invitations and write permissions. Smallest fix: accept the invitation, correct the URL, or sign in through Git’s authentication flow with the invited account. Organization policies may need admin help. Don’t make a private repository public to bypass access trouble.

Next: Build something small →
05 / MAKE15 min

Give the agent a finish line

In your verified clone, agree who is building first. One person drives while a teammate reviews. Copy this prompt into a new Codex task—not your terminal.

PASTE INTO CODEX
Build a small meeting-agenda tool in this repository for our MLD 371 team.

First inspect the repository and its instructions. Report your working folder and remote so I can confirm this is the right clone. Preserve existing work. Plan briefly, then create the actual files using plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with no frameworks, dependencies, API keys or external services.

The tool must add a named agenda item with positive whole-number minutes, remove individual items and show total duration. Reject blank or whitespace-only titles, blank minutes, zero, negative, nonnumeric, fractional or non-finite minutes with a clear message. Render titles as text, never as HTML. Use accessible labels, visible keyboard focus and a layout that works on a phone. Keep agenda data in memory; explain that reloading clears it.

Use index.html, style.css and script.js if those names are free. If they would overwrite existing work, stop and suggest a safe location. Explain how I can open index.html in a browser.

Check adding two items of 10 and 15 minutes totals 25, deleting the 10-minute item leaves 15, removing all items leaves 0, and invalid input is rejected without changing the list. Use available browser tools if possible. Fix problems and check again. Distinguish checks you actually ran from checks I still need to perform.

Explain the files changed, how the tool works and remaining limitations in plain language. Do not commit, push or publish. Leave the changes for human review.

Expected: real project files, a preview or opening instructions, and an honest account of checks.

If this fails: describe the observed behavior and expected result. Ask for one focused fix and a repeat of that check. If the folder is wrong, pause before edits and return to lesson 4.

Read any permission request before accepting it: the requested action should fit this small project. Ask for an explanation if it does not.

Next: Check it yourself →
06 / VERIFY10 min

“Done” is a claim. Try it.

An agent reporting success is different from you observing the result. Check these in your agenda tool. Mark only what you actually tried; these checkboxes do not run tests.

If a check fails: leave it unchecked. Tell Codex exactly what you entered, what happened and what should have happened. Retest after the fix. A partially checked list is useful evidence.

Next: Save & share →
07 / SHARE12 min

Move from your laptop to your team

Review the changed files in the app or editor before saving a snapshot. A diff shows what changed. New untracked files also need opening and review; git diff alone does not show their contents.

RUN IN THE PROJECT · POWERSHELL / TERMINAL
git status
git diff

Expected: only the changes you intend to share. If there are unrelated files or credentials, stop and exclude them before staging. Staging selects files for the next commit.

If Git asks who you are

Set a commit name and an email in this repository using the commands below. Replace both placeholders. For privacy, use the exact no-reply email shown in your GitHub email settings. These values label commits; they do not log you in.

EDIT FIRST · RUN IN POWERSHELL / TERMINAL
git config user.name "YOUR_NAME"
git config user.email "YOUR_GITHUB_NOREPLY_EMAIL"

GitHub commit email instructions

Commit, then push

For the three files in the exercise, run these one at a time after reviewing them. Adjust filenames if your tool used different ones. If a command fails, stop and read the message before continuing.

RUN IN THE PROJECT · POWERSHELL / TERMINAL
git add index.html style.css script.js
git diff --cached
git commit -m "Add tested meeting agenda tool"
git push
git log -1 --oneline
git status -sb

Expected: the commit creates a snapshot, push uploads it, and the GitHub branch shows the same latest commit as git log. Refresh the repository page and open the files there.

If this fails: for authentication, use lesson 4. If push says no upstream, run git branch --show-current, then git push -u origin YOUR_BRANCH with that actual branch name. If push is rejected because teammates pushed first, do not force-push; coordinate, pull their changes with a clean working tree and resolve any conflicts together.

GitHub push instructions

A low-conflict studio workflow

  1. Agree who edits which files. For this first tiny task, use one driver and one reviewer.
  2. Before starting another turn, confirm git status is clean, then run git pull --ff-only. If it refuses, pause and ask a teammate to help reconcile the branches.
  3. Make one small change, check it, commit, push and tell the next driver which branch to pull.
  4. When working simultaneously, create separate branches and open a pull request—a proposal to review and merge changes. Coordinate shared files before merging. GitHub flow.
Repository access is not website publication.

Your teammates can clone the files and open the agenda locally. A published website has a visitor URL and a separate hosting step. Private source access does not automatically make a published website private.

When your team is ready to publish a website

For a plain static project, GitHub Pages is a straightforward option: GitHub Free supports public repositories; eligible paid plans support private repositories. A Pages site is normally public even if its source is private. Never change visibility without your team’s agreement.

After agreeing on audience and reviewing content, a repository administrator can configure Pages. This tutorial’s own publication instructions are in its README. Visitors need no account for a public site. GitHub logs visitor IP addresses for security; the guide itself has no analytics. Pages availability and hosting privacy.

Next: Reflect on the process →
08 / REFLECT10 min

Keep a record of your judgment

Copy this note into your project documentation and fill it in yourself. “Not tested” is a valid answer. Do not turn an agent’s claims into checks you say you performed.

COPY INTO YOUR PROJECT NOTES · FILL IN YOURSELF
# AI methods note
Task: [What were we trying to make?]
Tool used: [App, model if known, and date]
AI contribution: [What did the agent create or change?]
Human decisions: [What did we choose, reject or revise, and why?]
Checks actually performed: [Inputs, expected results, observed results; who checked]
Failures or corrections: [What failed? What changed? What was checked again?]
Remaining limitations: [What is untested, incomplete or out of scope?]

Capability

Which part of the agenda tool could you now change yourself, and which still depends on the agent?

Power

Who on your team controls repository access and decides which suggested changes become the shared version?

Risk

If the total were wrong during a real meeting, who would notice—and what check would catch it beforehand?

Judgment

What did you accept or reject from the agent, and what evidence supported that decision?

You have a repeatable process.

Set a small goal. Let the agent work. Inspect the result. Verify behavior. Save and share intentionally. Keep the record of what you learned.
